source: "I'll pick you up at 8," he said to me.
correct: He told me he would pick me up at 8.
He told me that he would pick me up at 8.

source: "Leave the building immediately!" the officer said to us.
correct: The officer ordered us to leave the building immediately.
explanation: Órdenes en estilo indirecto: verbo introductorio + objeto + <to> + infinitivo.

source: "Could you please close the door?" she said to him.
correct: She asked him to close the door.
explanation: Peticiones en estilo indirecto: <asked> + objeto + <to> + infinitivo.

source: "Yes, I broke the vase," she said.
correct: She admitted breaking the vase.
She admitted that she had broken the vase.
explanation: <Admit> + gerundio o cláusula con <that> para confesiones.

source: "I didn't take the money," he said.
correct: He denied taking the money.
He denied having taken the money.
explanation: <Deny> + gerundio para negar algo. Nunca: <deny to + infinitivo>.

source: "Why don't we eat out tonight?" she said.
correct: She suggested eating out that night.
She suggested that they eat out that night.

source: "Don't touch that wire! It's dangerous," Dad said to me.
correct: Dad warned me not to touch that wire.
Dad warned me not to touch the wire because it was dangerous.
explanation: <Warn> + objeto + <not to> + infinitivo para advertencias negativas.

source: "I won't tell anyone your secret," she said.
correct: She promised not to tell anyone my secret.
She promised she wouldn't tell anyone my secret.

source: "You should try the seafood restaurant," he said.
correct: He recommended trying the seafood restaurant.
He recommended that I try the seafood restaurant.

source: "Don't forget to lock the door," Mum said to me.
correct: Mum reminded me to lock the door.

source: "You stole my idea!" she said to him.
correct: She accused him of stealing her idea.

source: "I'm sorry I forgot your birthday," he said.
correct: He apologized for forgetting my birthday.
He apologized for having forgotten my birthday.

source: "I'll pay for dinner. I insist," she said.
correct: She insisted on paying for dinner.

source: "Shall I carry your bags?" he said.
correct: He offered to carry my bags.

source: "No, I won't sign the contract," she said.
correct: She refused to sign the contract.

source: "OK, I'll work overtime this weekend," he said.
correct: He agreed to work overtime that weekend.

source: "The food here is always cold," she said.
correct: She complained that the food there was always cold.
She complained about the food always being cold.

source: "Go on, you can do it!" she said to him.
correct: She encouraged him to do it.
She encouraged him to go on.

source: "If you're late again, I'll fire you," the boss said.
correct: The boss threatened to fire me if I was late again.
The boss threatened to fire him if he was late again.

source: "Well done on passing your exam!" she said to me.
correct: She congratulated me on passing my exam.

source: "Where are you going tonight?" she asked me.
correct: She asked me where I was going that night.
explanation: Pregunta en estilo indirecto: orden de palabras de enunciado, cambio de tiempo verbal, cambio de referencias temporales.

source: "I've never been to that place before," he said.
correct: He claimed that he had never been to that place before.
He claimed he had never been to that place before.
explanation: <Claim> + cláusula con <that> para afirmaciones de veracidad dudosa.

source: "Please, please don't leave me!" she said.
correct: She begged me not to leave her.
explanation: <Beg> + objeto + <(not) to> + infinitivo para peticiones desesperadas.

source: "Would you like to come to my party on Saturday?" she said.
correct: She invited me to her party on Saturday.
She invited me to come to her party on Saturday.

source: "If I were you, I'd see a specialist," the doctor said.
correct: The doctor advised me to see a specialist.
